subtitle: Jaitugi of Devagiri and the Choice that Shaped the Eastern March

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a frontier landscape, Devagiri plateau fading west, distant Telangana plains east, with Jaitugi central between them
panels.action: Jaitugi Yadava stands in war cloak at the edge of a rocky escarpment, one hand resting on his sword hilt as he looks east over hazy plains and hill-forts, the setting sun splitting the sky between Devagiri and the far Kakatiya country.

dialogue.text: Hemadri sings that Jaitugi crushed the Kakatiyas and chained Ganapati—yet he chose to free his captive and rule the eastern frontier through him. Why did a conqueror release his defeated enemy?

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि गाता है कि जैतुगि ने काकतीयों को कुचला, गणपति को बेड़ियों में जकड़ा—पर उसने कैदी को छोड़ दिया, और उसी के जरिये पूरबी सीमा पर राज किया। विजेता ने हारे दुश्मन को क्यों आज़ाद किया?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Jaitugi in council chamber at Devagiri, map-strewn stone floor
panels.action: Inside a dim hall at Devagiri, Jaitugi sits on a simple lion-backed seat, leaning forward as courtiers lay palm-leaf maps on the floor showing western coasts, southern plateaus and the vague eastern tracts of Telangana.

dialogue.text: In the late twelfth century, Devagiri’s Yadavas faced a harsh truth: the west was restless, the south uncertain, and the east—toward the Kakatiya country—lay half-known, yet full of rival claims and shifting loyalties.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के अंत में देवगिरी के यादवों पर कड़वी सच्चाई साफ थी: पश्चिम बेचैन, दक्षिण डावाँडोल, और पूरब—काकती देश की ओर—आधा जाना, पर दावों से भरा, निष्ठाएँ हर पल बदलतीं।

panels.shot: wide bird's-eye over Deccan plateau showing multiple power centers marked by forts
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Deccan: stony hills dotted with forts, banners of different colours rising over distant strongholds, suggesting Yadava, Hoysala and Kakatiya spheres without explicit emblems.

dialogue.text: Yadavas at Devagiri, Hoysalas near Dorasamudra, and the rising Kakatiyas around Warangal watched one another across rugged lands. No border was neat; frontier was a living, contested space.

i18n.hi: देवगिरी के यादव, दोरसमुद्र के पास होयसाल, और वरंगल के उठते काकती एक-दूजे को ऊबड़ देस के पार ताकते रहे। कोई सीमा सीधी न थी; सरहद खुद चलती-लड़ती जगह थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, Jaitugi listening intently to a messenger from the south
panels.action: A dust-covered messenger, hands pressed in respectful greeting, leans toward Jaitugi, speaking urgently, as attendants listen in tense silence beneath carved stone pillars.

dialogue.text: Hemadri’s praise hints that Jaitugi first faced trouble on his southern flank, with Hoysala pressure near his borders. When that crisis ebbed, his attention turned, deliberately, toward the east.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि के गुणगान से झलकता है कि जैतुगि को पहले दक्षिणी तरफ होयसाल दबाव से झटके लगे। जब वो आँधी थमी, उसने सोच-समझकर रुख पूरब की ओर मोड़ा।

panels.shot: close-up on Hemadri’s imagined hand writing with stylus on palm leaf beside an image of Jaitugi
panels.action: A stylus etches small, precise letters on a palm leaf as a miniature painting of Jaitugi in battle takes shape beside the text, suggesting Hemadri composing dynastic eulogy.

dialogue.text: In his Chaturvarga Chintamani, Hemadri calls Jaitugi a lion who shattered the Kakatiya line, mentions a Raudra whose head was taken, and speaks of Ganapati seized like a captive elephant.

i18n.hi: अपने ‘चतुर्वर्ग चिंतामणि’ में हेमाद्रि जैतुगि को सिंह कहता है, जिसने काकती वंश तोड़ दिया; एक ‘रौद्र’ का सिर लिया गया, और गणपति को बंधे हाथों वाले हाथी सा पकड़ा गया।

panels.shot: thoughtful close-up on Jaitugi’s face lit by lamplight, eyes turned toward the east-facing doorway
panels.action: By a single oil lamp, Jaitugi sits in quiet reflection near an open doorway that frames the dark eastern horizon, his features calm but resolved, hand resting on a rolled campaign order.

dialogue.text: Around 1191–1198 CE, he chose to march east. The campaign would test not only his force of arms, but the way Devagiri would hold its farthest lands.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1191–1198 ई. में उसने पूरब को चढ़ाई चुनी। यह मुहिम सिर्फ उसकी तलवार नहीं, देवगिरी की दूर की ज़मीनें संभालने की ताकत भी आजमाती।

panels.shot: epic wide of Yadava host moving east across rocky plains
panels.action: Jaitugi rides at the head of a long column of horsemen and foot soldiers crossing a stony plateau, dust rising as banners stream behind them, distant hills hinting at the approach to Telangana.

dialogue.text: Columns of Yadava cavalry and infantry moved out from Devagiri. Their path led through dry uplands and river valleys toward the Kakatiya country, where hill-forts guarded the way.

i18n.hi: यादव घुड़सवार और पैदल टुकड़ियाँ देवगिरी से चलीं। रास्ता सूखे पठारों, नदी घाटियों से होकर काकती देश तक गया, जहाँ पहाड़ी किले राह रोकते थे।

panels.shot: tense wide of a Kakatiya hill-fort silhouette facing the approaching army
panels.action: A rugged hill-fort rises against the sky, its stone walls outlined in the morning light as the Yadava army appears on the opposite ridge, both sides poised in hard silence before contact.

dialogue.text: Hemadri speaks of fort after fort subdued, a frontier pushed back. He names a Raudra fallen in battle, but the record stays silent on whether this was Rudradeva or Mahadeva.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि एक-एक किले के दबने, सीमा पीछे खिसकने की बात करता है। वह एक ‘रौद्र’ के रण में गिरने का नाम लेता है, पर शिला-लिखत चुप हैं कि वो रुद्रदेव था या महादेव।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Jaitugi in battle posture without showing gore
panels.action: On a smoky hillside, Jaitugi stands in the thick of combat with raised sword, surrounded by clashing shields and rearing horses, faces set with strain but no wounds visible.

dialogue.text: The clash was fierce. Hemadri’s panegyric makes it blazing and absolute; modern scholars read through the praise to see a hard-fought border war, not an annihilated kingdom.

i18n.hi: टक्कर विकट थी। हेमाद्रि की स्तुति इसे धधकती, अंतिम बनाती है; आज के विद्वान उसके गीतों के पार देखते हैं—यह एक सख्त सरहदी जंग थी, मिटा दी गयी रियासत नहीं।

panels.shot: slow motion-like close-up of Ganapati being led bound but unharmed into Jaitugi’s presence
panels.action: In the aftermath, a dignified young Ganapati is brought into Jaitugi’s camp with his hands loosely bound, flanked by guards but treated with visible respect, as Jaitugi rises to receive him.

dialogue.text: From inscriptions and Hemadri’s words comes a stark image: Ganapati Deva taken captive. For a moment, the eastern frontier lay in Jaitugi’s hands, its chief prisoner before him.

i18n.hi: शिला-लेखों और हेमाद्रि की बातों से एक कड़ा चित्र उभरता है: गणपति देव बंदी बना लिए गए। एक पल को पूरबी सरहद जैतुगि की मुट्ठी में थी, उसका सरदार कैदी सामने।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Jaitugi and Ganapati seated opposite each other in a tent, guards outside
panels.action: Inside a campaign tent, Jaitugi sits composed on a rug while Ganapati, no longer bound, faces him across a low table, both men guarded but calm, the air heavy with decision.

dialogue.speaker: jaitugi
dialogue.text: Rule your land, Ganapati—under Devagiri’s shadow, not against it.

i18n.hi: “अपना देस चला गणपति—देवगिरी की छाया में, उसके खिलाफ नहीं।”

panels.shot: wide shot of a palm-leaf treaty being placed between them, hands from both sides touching it
panels.action: A palm leaf inscribed with grants and obligations lies between Jaitugi and Ganapati, as each extends a hand toward it, implying acceptance of overlordship and vassalage, attendants watching closely.

dialogue.text: The evidence is clear on the outcome: Ganapati ruled, but as a subordinate. Early Kakatiya inscriptions acknowledge Yadava overlordship, even as they continue to build local power.

i18n.hi: नतीजा साफ दिखता है: गणपति ने राज किया, पर अधीन बनकर। शुरुआती काकती शिला-लेख यादव प्रभुत्व मानते हैं, साथ ही अपनी स्थानीय ताकत भी गढ़ते रहते हैं।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of rugged Telangana countryside with scattered forts and villages
panels.action: An expansive view of Telangana’s rough terrain: broken hills, forest patches, scattered forts and villages, suggesting the difficulty of direct control from distant Devagiri.

dialogue.text: Cynthia Talbot and P.V.P. Sastry read the frontier differently from Hemadri’s poems: the land was diverse, distant, and resistant to direct rule from Devagiri’s plateau.

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टैलबॉट और पी.वी.पी. सास्त्री सीमा को हेमाद्रि की कविताओं से अलग पढ़ते हैं: ये देस रंग-बिरंगा, दूर, और देवगिरी के पठार से सीधी हुकूमत के खिलाफ था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jaitugi in council, advisers gesturing toward east on a map
panels.action: Back at Devagiri, Jaitugi sits with advisers over a floor-map; one points to the east with a stick while another gestures to the limited troops, Jaitugi listening, hand thoughtfully at his beard.

dialogue.text: Jaitugi’s choice not to occupy Telangana directly was practical. Distance, terrain and limited manpower made vassalage—rather than full incorporation—the workable way to hold the frontier.

i18n.hi: जैतुगि का तेलंगाना पर सीधे क़ब्ज़ा न करना समझौता नहीं, दूरदर्शी फैसला था। दूरी, धरती और कम जनशक्ति ने वफादार जागीरदारी को—पूरा विलय नहीं—सरहद संभालने का रास्ता बनाया।

panels.shot: split-scene style: Devagiri court on one side, Ganapati’s court on the other, both functioning
panels.action: Visually divided frame: on the left, Jaitugi presides over Devagiri’s stone-pillared court; on the right, Ganapati holds court in a Kakatiya hall, each surrounded by local chiefs, echoing a layered hierarchy.

dialogue.text: For some years, overlord and vassal coexisted: Yadava suzerainty above, Kakatiya authority below. The frontier was held not by Yadava administrators, but by a local ruler bound by obligation.

i18n.hi: कुछ बरसों तक मालिक और जागीरदार साथ रहे: ऊपर यादव प्रभुता, नीचे काकती हुकूमत। सरहद यादव अफसरों से नहीं, एक बंधे हुए स्थानीय शासक से थामी गई।

panels.shot: close-up of a Kakatiya inscription being chiselled, with the faint mention of Yadava overlordship
panels.action: A stonecutter chisels lines into a pillar, as a supervising priest traces letters that include a reference to a higher power, hinting at Yadava overlordship within a Kakatiya record.

dialogue.text: Garavapada and other early Ganapati inscriptions speak of grants and titles under overlords. Through these dry lines of stone, the political compromise becomes visible.

i18n.hi: गरवापद और दूसरे शुरुआती गणपति शिला-लेख जागीरें और उपाधियाँ ऊपर के मालिकों के नाम से लिखते हैं। इन्हीं सूखे पत्थर की पंक्तियों से सियासी समझौता दिखने लगता है।

panels.shot: wide shot over later Warangal fort, suggesting rising Kakatiya strength against distant Devagiri
panels.action: A later, more massive hill-fort with intricate gateways rises under the Kakatiya landscape, while far off, barely visible on the horizon, lies the suggestion of Devagiri’s plateau.

dialogue.text: In time, Ganapati and his successors would grow stronger, challenging overlords old and new. Yet the memory of Yadava suzerainty marks an early phase of Kakatiya ascent.

i18n.hi: आगे चलकर गणपति और उनके उत्तराधिकारी ताकतवर हुए, पुराने-नए मालिकों को चुनौती दी। पर यादव प्रभुता की याद काकती उभार के शुरुआती पड़ाव पर निशान छोड़ जाती है।

panels.shot: reflective close-up on Jaitugi in older age, looking at both an unsheathed sword and a sealed document
panels.action: An older Jaitugi sits quietly, gaze moving between an unsheathed sword laid on the floor and a sealed palm-leaf grant set beside it, his expression steady, weighed by past campaigns and choices.

dialogue.text: Hemadri remembers Jaitugi for the blow against the Kakatiyas. The frontier remembers him for something quieter: the decision to hold power with a released enemy, not a distant, strained occupation.

i18n.hi: हेमाद्रि जैतुगि को काकतीयों पर पड़े घात के लिए याद रखता है। सरहद उसे एक और बात से याद करती है: छूटे दुश्मन के सहारे ताकत पकड़ने का फैसला, दूर, थकी हुई फौजी हुकूमत नहीं।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Deccan from high above, borders invisible, routes and forts forming a web
panels.action: From far above, the Deccan stretches in all directions, roads and rivers weaving between forts and cities, no clear borders drawn, only a web of ties, oaths and shifting strengths.

dialogue.text: Jaitugi’s eastward march shows a frontier not as a line on a map, but as a living choice: when to advance, when to let another rule, and how power can rest on restraint as much as on conquest.

i18n.hi: जैतुगि की पूरबी चढ़ाई दिखाती है कि सरहद नक्शे की लकीर नहीं, जीती हुई चुन है—कब बढ़ना, कब किसी और को राज करने देना, और कैसे कभी ताकत रोके रखने से भी टिकती है, सिर्फ जीत से नहीं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Jaitugi of Devagiri and the Choice that Shaped the Eastern March
subtitle_i18n.hi: देवगिरी के जैतुगि और फैसला जिसने पूरबी चढ़ाई बदल दी
